headline: Telangana HC: Additional Commissioner valid proper officer for GST orders above ₹2 crore
reference: M/s UBV Infrastructures Ltd. v. Union of India & others, WP No. 37085 of 2026, Telangana High Court, order dated 18.11.2026
summary_points: Issue: writ challenging an Order-in-Original of 18.09.2025 imposing Section 122(2) CGST/TGST penalties for Dec 2018 to Jun 2022, on grounds of improper officer and no hearing.
Held: SCN was issued by a Joint Commissioner and the order passed by an Additional Commissioner, who ranks above the proper officer for cases over ₹2 crore; jurisdiction plea rejected.
Held: portal service of the order is valid under Section 169(1)(d) as relied on by the Department; the writ, filed on 17.10.2026, was far beyond the appeal limitation period.
Following Glaxo Smith Kline (SC), the Court found no exceptional circumstances for Article 226 relief; overlapping proceedings and factual disputes belong before the appellate forum.
Writ dismissed with liberty to file an appeal before the competent forum, to be decided on merits.
who_is_affected: Taxpayers facing GST adjudication orders, especially those served only through the GST portal, and professionals advising on writ versus appeal remedies.
action_required: Track appeal limitation from the date of portal upload and file statutory appeals on time rather than relying on writ petitions challenging jurisdiction or service.

Telangana High Court dismisses writ challenging a GST penalty order: M/s UBV Infrastructures Ltd. v. Union of India (WP No. 37085 of 2026, decided 18.11.2026).

The petitioner challenged an Order-in-Original dated 18.09.2025 imposing penalties under Section 122(2) of the CGST/TGST Acts for December 2018 to June 2022. It argued that the officer was not the proper officer and that the proceedings overlapped with State orders.

The Court held:
- The SCN was issued by a Joint Commissioner and the order was passed by an Additional Commissioner, a higher rank, in a case above ₹2 crore. The jurisdiction plea failed.
- The order was served through the GST portal, which the Court treated as valid service.
- Following the Supreme Court's decision in Glaxo Smith Kline, a writ filed long after the appeal period cannot be entertained without exceptional circumstances.
- Factual disputes and overlapping proceedings must be raised in the statutory appeal.

The petitioner has been given liberty to file an appeal.

Takeaway: check the GST portal regularly and calendar appeal deadlines from the date of upload.

Please verify the details with the official judgment before relying on this update.
